title: A salary run that cannot go wrong
summary: Pay 40,000 employees on the last working day, correctly, even when the bank has a bad morning.
context: Ragi Payroll pays salaries for 700 companies. On the last working day, each company approves a file, and transfers go out through a bank's API, with limits on how many per minute. A bank's API may time out, leaving no way to tell if the transfer happened.
Companies approve at the last moment. People notice instantly when their salary is late, and a double payment is very hard to recover.
must_handle: No employee is paid twice, even after timeouts and restarts.
A company's run can be paused or corrected after approval until money moves.
One company's bad file does not hold up the others.
A bank's outage leads to a sensible retry, with the affected companies told.
Every rupee can be accounted for at the end of the day.
show_in_answer: The states of a run, and of one payment within it.
How a timeout with an unknown result is resolved.
How the work is paced against the bank's limits.
What a company's payroll officer sees during the run.
